summary: Framework-free REST liveness/readiness probe dispatch and Kubernetes probe path alignment for messenger, mail, social, and community backbone services.
claim_boundary: This slice adds framework-free REST probe dispatch for /health and /ready plus static Kubernetes probe path alignment. It does not bind Hyper, run Kubernetes, prove live ArgoCD health, execute downstream dependency checks, or claim production readiness.

best_practice_research.used_for: Dedicated minimal HTTP probe endpoints and readiness/liveness separation.
HTTP probe status-code behavior and readiness failure semantics.

source_basis.use: Existing messenger REST route catalog, contract-only dispatcher, write-route dispatcher, and OpenAPI /health + /ready contract entries.
Existing mail REST route catalog and write-route dispatcher now extended with probe routes.
Existing social REST route catalog, contract-only dispatcher, write-route dispatcher, and OpenAPI /health + /ready contract entries.
Existing community REST route catalog and write-route dispatcher now extended with probe routes.
Existing Helm readiness/liveness probes previously referenced undeclared /healthz and /livez paths.

findings: Each REST crate gets small enum/struct probe dispatch without introducing a web framework, JSON parser, Kubernetes client, or provider SDK.
Kubernetes probe paths now match declared service REST probe routes, reducing later ArgoCD/Kubernetes deployment risk while keeping readiness dependency evidence explicit and caller-supplied.
Tests cover healthy liveness, ready and not-ready readiness, non-probe known-route refusal, and unknown-route refusal for all four services.
F3_adversarial.not_applicable_reason: Probe handlers are new bounded surfaces rather than a regression fix; tests cover liveness, ready, not-ready, non-probe known route, and unknown route behavior for each REST crate.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Readiness returns 503 when any caller-supplied dependency is not ready and 200 only when all are ready.

findings: Future Hyper/Kubernetes runtime binding gets explicit /health and /ready entrypoints with small typed responses instead of inferring from business write-route dispatch.
Focused REST tests/check/clippy/fmt, OpenAPI YAML parsing, and static probe-path grep validate the slice.
Chose /health + /ready to match existing messenger/social contracts and Kubernetes readiness/liveness semantics instead of retaining undeclared /healthz and /livez Helm paths.
Chose caller-supplied dependency readiness evidence over fake live dependency checks while no Hyper/Kubernetes runtime exists.
alternatives_named: Add fake live dependency checks in REST crates
Align contracts, REST catalogs, and Helm probes around /health and /ready
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The selected path aligns static deployment config with declared REST probe routes while preserving honest non-claims about live runtime evidence.
rejected_reasons: Undeclared Helm paths would fail once bound to the current REST catalog.
Fake dependency checks would overclaim readiness without a runtime.

findings: Probe responses contain service status metadata only; they do not expose tenant identifiers, request bodies, principals, secrets, or downstream connection strings.
Probe responses are minimal typed metadata and avoid dependency calls in liveness; readiness folds over caller-supplied dependency booleans only.
The change improves operational compliance posture by making Kubernetes readiness/liveness routes explicit, but does not claim live audit, branch-protection, certification, or SLO evidence.
Mail/community OpenAPI contracts now expose the same probe route shape as messenger/social.
Reverting this slice removes probe handlers, OpenAPI additions for mail/community, and Helm path changes without touching API/usecase/app/persistence behavior.
Readiness dependency names provide low-cardinality status evidence for future metrics/log binding, but this slice does not emit telemetry.
Existing business REST write route behavior is unchanged; contract-only non-probe endpoints still return 501 through the existing dispatcher. Helm probe path changes are static and reversible.
Probe route constants use existing REST crate naming style and public routes match existing /health and /ready vocabulary.
tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain evidence document scope, verification, and non-claims.
REST boundary changes stay inside REST crates; Kubernetes path alignment stays inside microservice Helm deployment templates; OpenAPI additions stay in microservice contracts.
No domain/usecase/app/persistence layers import REST or Kubernetes concerns; probe dispatch remains framework-free at the REST boundary.
No dependencies were added or moved.
Readiness algorithm is deterministic all-dependencies-ready folding; liveness intentionally ignores dependencies and documents its non-claim.
Touched REST crates and Helm paths are covered by existing backbone CI/Jenkins path matrices; local focused checks passed while remote Actions remains budget-blocked.

non_claims: No Hyper/axum/tonic HTTP server binding, JSON serialization, Kubernetes pod execution, ArgoCD sync, or live cloud deployment is implemented by this slice.
Readiness dependency status is caller-supplied framework-free evidence; no live SQL, outbox, policy, OTel collector, broker, or service-mesh dependency was contacted.

Contract-only business endpoints remain contract-only; this slice only implements liveness/readiness probe routes.
